title: Checkpoint: The Last Cases and the Three Tenses
summary: A cumulative examination of sections eleven to fourteen: the instrumental and the vocative that complete the declension, the numerals with the hour and the date, and the past and future that complete the indicative.

drills.stem: What is the instrumental singular of **katė**?
drills.explanation: The **-ė** declension makes its instrumental in **-e**: *kate*. *katei* is the dative, *katėje* the locative, *katės* the genitive.

drills.stem: How would you address **mokytojas**?
drills.explanation: Agent nouns in *-ojas* and *-ėjas* take **-au** in the vocative. *mokytojai* is the nominative plural; an ordinary noun in *-as* would give *-e*, but this class does not.

drills.stem: Which of these correctly use the instrumental?
drills.explanation: A means takes the bare instrumental (*autobusu*), company takes *su* with it (*su draugu*). A pencil is a means and wants no *su*; *sirgti* governs the instrumental, so it must be *sergu gripu*.

drills.stem: **Knyga po stalu.** What does the instrumental tell you here?
options: That the book is a means.
That *po* means *under*, of place, rather than *after*, of time.
That the book belongs to the table.
That the sentence is in the past.
drills.explanation: *Po* governs two cases with two meanings: instrumental for *under*, genitive for *after*. Only the ending distinguishes *po stalu* from *po pietų*.

drills.stem: Complete: **Rašau ____.** (I am writing to my friends.)
drills.explanation: The dative plural ends in **-ms**: *draugams*. *draugais* is the instrumental plural — with friends, not to them.

drills.stem: In **Savaitgaliais važiuoju traukiniu pas brolį**, how many words stand in the instrumental?
drills.explanation: Two: *savaitgaliais*, a plural instrumental of recurring time, and *traukiniu*, the means. *pas brolį* is a preposition with the accusative and has nothing to do with the case.

drills.stem: Which is **Friday**?
drills.explanation: The days count from Monday as the first, so the fifth day is *penktadienis*. Only *sekmadienis* stands outside the pattern.

drills.stem: Complete: **Čia yra ____ kėdės.** (There are four chairs here.)
drills.explanation: *kėdė* is feminine, and the numerals one to nine agree in gender: **keturios**. *ketvirtos* would be the ordinal, *the fourth*.

drills.stem: **Be penkiolikos dešimta.** What time is it?
drills.explanation: Literally *without fifteen, the tenth* — a quarter before ten, that is 9:45. The hour named is the one being counted towards, exactly as in *pusė dešimtos* for half past nine.

drills.stem: Which of these are **correct**?
drills.explanation: From ten upwards a numeral fixes its noun in the genitive plural (*minučių*); from one to nine it agrees, so a nominative plural *minutės* follows *trys*.

drills.stem: **Londone buvau savaitę.** What does the accusative *savaitę* express?
options: The day on which he arrived.
drills.explanation: The accusative of time covers both a point and a stretch; here it is duration, and no word answering to English *for* is used.

drills.stem: Which is correct for **on the tenth of May**?
drills.explanation: The month goes into the genitive and the day into the ordinal; because the phrase says *when*, the ordinal takes the accusative of time: *gegužės dešimtą*.

drills.stem: Which preposition of time takes the **accusative**?
drills.explanation: *prieš valandą*, an hour ago, and *per valandą*, within an hour, both take the accusative. *po*, *iki* and *nuo* all take the genitive.

drills.stem: **gyventi, gyvena, gyveno.** What is *we lived*?
drills.explanation: The third principal part *gyveno* is an *-o* past, so the first person plural is **gyvenome**. *gyvename* is the present.

drills.stem: **matyti, mato, matė.** What is *I saw*?
drills.explanation: An *-ė* past takes **-iau**, and the *-iau* softens the preceding **t** to *č*: *mačiau*. *matau* is the present.

drills.stem: Which of these are correct past forms of **būti**?
drills.explanation: *esu* is the present. *būti* is perfectly regular in the past, taking the *-o* endings on *buvo*, and unlike the present it can never be left out.

drills.stem: Complete: **Vakar nevalgiau ____.** (Yesterday I did not eat the bread.)
drills.explanation: A negated verb takes its object in the genitive, and the past tense alters nothing: *duonos*. Losing the genitive of negation when the tense changes is a standing trap.

drills.stem: *Dirbau* can render three English tenses. Which three?
options: I work, I shall work, I would work.
I worked, I was working, I have worked.
I work, I am working, I have worked.
I had worked, I would have worked, I work.
drills.explanation: Lithuanian has one past where English divides into simple, continuous and perfect. An adverb or the context supplies whatever difference is wanted.

drills.stem: What is the future of **skaityti** in the first person singular?
drills.explanation: Infinitive stem *skaity-* plus **-s-** plus **-iu**: *skaitysiu*. *skaitys* is the third person, *skaičiau* the past.

drills.stem: In which of these does the stem alter before the **-s-** of the future?
drills.explanation: *grįž-* absorbs the marker to give *grįš-*, and *ved-* has its d turn to s. A vowel stem like *kalbė-* and a stem in b like *dirb-* are untouched.

drills.stem: Complete: **Rytoj nepirksiu šios ____.** (Tomorrow I shall not buy this book.)
drills.explanation: The genitive of negation holds in every tense, the future included: *knygos*, with *šios* agreeing in the genitive beside it. A learner who writes *knygą* has carried the affirmative construction across the negative.

drills.title: Pernai ir kitąmet
drills.passage: Pernai birželį mes buvome Klaipėdoje. Važiavome traukiniu; kelionė truko keturias valandas. Ten gyvenome savaitę, valgėme žuvį ir kasdien ėjome prie jūros. Vakarais buvo vėsu, todėl nešiojau striukę. Aš nepirkau suvenyrų — pinigų buvo mažai. Kitą vasarą grįšime; važiuosime autobusu, nes bilietai bus pigesni, ir būsime ten dvi savaites.
drills.translation: Last year in June we were in Klaipėda. We travelled by train; the journey took four hours. We lived there for a week, ate fish and went to the sea every day. In the evenings it was cool, so I wore a jacket. I did not buy any souvenirs — there was little money. Next summer we shall return; we shall go by bus, because the tickets will be cheaper, and we shall be there for two weeks.

questions.explanation: *Pernai birželį mes buvome Klaipėdoje* — a locative of place with the past of *būti*, which unlike the present can never be omitted.

questions.stem: Which statements about the last sentence of the passage are correct?
options: *grįšime* shows a stem whose final consonant merged with the -s- marker.
*važiuosime* keeps its stem unchanged because it ends in a vowel.
*bus* is the third person and would be the same for a plural subject.
*dvi savaites* is a genitive of quantity.
questions.explanation: *dvi savaites* is an **accusative** of duration: the numeral agrees with its noun, and the phrase says how long. A genitive would appear only after a numeral of ten or more.

questions.stem: How many **future** verb forms does the passage contain?
questions.explanation: Four: *grįšime*, *važiuosime*, *bus* and *būsime*. Everything before the last sentence is past, and the whole of the future is marked by the one letter **s** between stem and ending.
